core_thesis: Calculus provides tools to analyze and interpret the behavior of functions through graphical, limit-based, and derivative methods.
supporting_theses: Graphs provide visual insights into the nature and behavior of functions by plotting input-output pairs.
The slope of a curve at a point is defined through the concept of limits as the secant line approaches a tangent line.
The derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change of a function at any point on its curve.
problems: What are the fundamental concepts in calculus that help us understand functions?
How do we measure rates of change and slopes of curves?
questions: What are the fundamental concepts in calculus that help us understand functions?

assumptions: Exact methods for determining the smoothness of curves in complex cases are not fully addressed.
